title: Detangle latency — evening scratchpad
content:
Evening quick dump — observed increased p95/p99 generation latency for hosted-api (us-west-2) starting ~18:20 PST. Not GPU this time; packet-level skew/RTT spikes look suspicious. Writing down next actions and command snippets so I don't forget while on-call.

What I saw (timeline):
- 18:15 small spike in 95th token latency on /v1/generate route (console traces).
- 18:20 sustained p95 ~420ms (previous baseline ~120ms). p99 hitting ~1.2s periodically.
- 18:28 Traces show tail at network hop between svc-edge-nginx and node pool (pod -> host).
- 18:35 Alerts: net-queue-length high for nic ens5 on node usw2-node-47.

Hypotheses (quick):
- NIC interrupt storms or driver regression after kernel patch (check dmesg).
- Link-level errors (cable/TOPO flaps) or ECMP path asymmetry to a specific AZ spine.
- TC (traffic control) shaping or kube-proxy conntrack exhaustion.
- Application-level congestion (bursty batching) — but traces point to hop-level latency not model time.

Immediate triage steps (do these in order):
1) Narrow to node and pod: kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide --field-selector spec.nodeName=usw2-node-47
2) Check node NIC stats: sudo ethtool -S ens5 | egrep "rx_errors|tx_errors|rx_over_errors|tx_aborted_errors"
3) dmesg | tail -n 200 (look for NIC driver messages, soft/hard reset notices)
4) tc qdisc show dev ens5 ; tc -s qdisc show dev ens5 (queue drop counters)
5) netstat -s | egrep "Tcp:|Ip:" (quick sanity)
6) curl to local edge from within node: curl -sS -w '%{time_connect} %{time_starttransfer}\n' -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
7) If link errors or driver resets -> open ENGINF-1423 and mark node for hardware follow-up.

Quick mitigations to keep traffic healthy:
- If node NIC flapping: cordon + drain (graceful) and let autoscaler spin replacement. Commands: kubectl cordon usw2-node-47 ; kubectl drain usw2-node-47 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force --grace-period=120
- If conntrack exhaustion suspected: sudo sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max (compare) and clear conntrack for specific flows (conntrack -L | grep <ip> ; conntrack -D --orig-src <ip>) — do carefully.
- Reroute by updating service routing: scale up node pool in another AZ (usw2-nodepool-b) for short window.

Notes to follow-up after stabilizing:
- Check for any kernel updates rolled 03/01 that might correlate. (pkg: linux-5.15.88 -> linux-5.15.92)
- Run nic firmware health check with infra-hw team: serial 1ZXY-... (need to collect SFP counters).
- Add a short test in canary agent: synthetic 100 concurrent light requests across AZs, capture per-hop latencies, upload pcap for 30s.

Repro steps to run locally (min):
- Spin up two nodes in staging, enable iperf3 between pods on different hosts, run bursty UDP to test for packet drops: iperf3 -c <peer> -u -b 200M -t 60
- Run tc to simulate latency/jitter: sudo tc qdisc add dev ens5 root netem delay 50ms 10ms distribution normal

Random quick ops commands I used tonight (save for runbook):
- kubectl top node usw2-node-47
- kubectl logs -n redwood edge-proxy-abcde --since=10m | grep "upstream response time"
- sudo dmesg | egrep "eth|mlx|nic|vfio|firmware" --color=auto

Open todo for me (short):
- [ ] Push notes to Confluence page and link INC/ENGINF IDs. (low)
- [ ] Add synthetic test to canary suite (Lina to review) (mid)
- [ ] Confirm kernel package rollback plan with release-eng if we see reproducible driver regression (high)
- [ ] Schedule physical port check with infra-hw on Mon morning (Marcus)

Random thoughts / questions to ask Lina/Marcus:
- Lina: did we roll anything to edge-proxy hostpool yesterday afternoon? (I saw a little spike in small deploys at 16:30).
- Marcus: can infra-hw dump SFP counters from the leafs that host usw2?

If things degrade while I'm troubleshooting:
- Failover idea: set routing policy to prefer us-east-1 for low-latency customers temporarily (needs on-call approval + release notes).
- Short-term knob: reduce max_batch_size for hosted-api route to reduce head-of-line blocking for slow nodes.

End-of-shift handoff (what to tell next on-call):
- State: node usw2-node-47 suspected NIC-level errors; p95 elevated.
- Locked actions done: looked at dmesg, checked tc counters, created ENGINF-1423 (link above).
- Next: coordinate removal of node from pool if flapping continues; Lina to check canary traces; Marcus to confirm hardware counters.

Misc bookmark: commands/refs I want in runbook later:
- conntrack -L | grep <pod-ip>
- sudo ethtool -S ens5 | egrep "errors|drops|reset"
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | egrep "evict|oom|failed to"

— Arjun

(End scratchpad)
